newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rebels strike again, kill policeman, wife.
newsitem.headline: Indian rebels strike again, kill policeman, wife.

text.p: A senior Indian police officer and his wife died on Monday when their vehicle hit a landmine which police said was planted by a group of left-wing extremists who killed 14 people in a daring attack last week.

The mine exploded as the van drove over a culvert in the southern state of Andhra Pradesh, killing deputy police superintendent Mahesh Kumar and his wife, and injuring three other policemen, police officer K.L. Reddy told Reuters.

Police said the landmine was planted by the outlawed People's War Group (PWG), the same Maoist rebels which killed 13 policemen and a civilian last Friday in a raid on a village police station in Adilabad district in Andhra Pradesh.

Monday's explosion occurred at 6:30 a.m. (0100 GMT) near Ranapur town, 130 km (80 miles) east of the state capital Hyderabad. Last Friday's attack took place in Sirpuru village, 260 km (160 miles) from the capital.
The PWG is one of many Maoist rebel groups considered part of the Naxalite movement, which started in India in the 1960s among groups who split from the main communist party.
It was first banned in Andhra Pradesh in 1992 but gained a year-long reprieve beginning in June 1995 before being banned again in July of this year.
